entries.title: Critical alerts get buried under low-severity noise in the alert queue
entries.statement: The alert queue carries high volume with few relevant alerts, so critical alerts on important assets end up below large numbers of low-severity alerts, often PowerShell noise from test boxes. Examples: a critical alert waited 40 minutes at night, a credential dump on DC-01 waited 20 minutes, one account opened 40 alerts to find 3 that mattered, and a Helix screenshot shows 12 low PowerShell alerts on top. Engineering says most triage time is spent digging through the queue, not investigating.

evidence.quote: Honestly the queue is the pain. On a bad day we get two, three hundred alerts and maybe ten matter.
A low on a test box should never be above a critical on a domain controller.
A critical alert on our file server sat in the queue for 40 minutes on the night shift.
It was below 60 low alerts from a scanner.
Most of that time is analysts digging through the queue, not the investigation itself.
we opened 40 alerts to find the 3 that mattered
Northwind ticket NW-2340: a credential dump on DC-01 sat in the queue for 20 min under PowerShell noise from a test box. Their CISO is now involved.
Helix ticket HX-102: same 'can't find the critical alerts' complaint.
Attaching their screenshot of a queue page with 12 low-severity PowerShell alerts on top.

conflicts.summary: D-12 (active) says only incident leads may run containment and forbids enabling the button for analysts or bypassing the API check. On 2026-10-08 the PM decided in Slack that analysts can isolate test-tagged assets, but D-12 has not been updated and has no test-asset exception.
conflicts.question: Is D-12 being amended to let analysts isolate test-tagged assets? If so, who approves the change, how is 'test' tagging verified so a mis-tagged production host can't be isolated, and will the decision log be updated before any work starts?

conflicts.summary: D-07 (active) requires analysts to see every ingested alert and forbids dropping or permanently hiding alerts. On 2026-10-01 Head of Product decided in Slack to hide duplicates by default for Acme (latest per fingerprint, toggle to show all). Engineering flagged a clash, Support noted Northwind's auditors check that nothing is hidden by default (K-046), and design asked not to ship it until D-07 is settled (K-047). The decision log has not been updated.
conflicts.question: Does hiding duplicates by default behind a toggle comply with D-07 and the SOC 2 requirement? If yes, should D-07 be amended to say so, and is it Acme-only or global given Northwind's audit check? If no, would grouping duplicates into one visible row with a count (K-008) meet Acme's need instead?

conflicts.summary: D-15 (active) says no new navigation items 'this quarter' while navigation research runs. On 2026-08-29 Head of Product quoted D-15 as 'no new top-level nav this year'. The scope in Slack is longer than the written decision.
conflicts.question: Does D-15 run to the end of the quarter or the end of the year? If it was extended, can the decision log be updated with the new end date?
